Rashi on Menachot 109a:11:1.hebrew: ואמר ליה רב המנונא: נזיר, הוי ודאי טעמא כדקאמרת, דלא חל עליה שם נזירות. אבל עולה, היינו טעמא: נעשה כאומר וכו', ושם עולה עליה, וחייב כרת:
Rashi on Menachot 109a:11:1.english: And Rav Hamnuna [could] say to him: [In the case of a] nazirite, the reason is certainly as you said, that the status of naziriteship does not take effect upon him. But [as for] an olah [burnt offering], this is the reason: he is considered as one who says, etc., and the status of an olah is upon it, and [therefore] he is liable to karet [for slaughtering outside the Temple].

Rashi on Menachot 109a:12:1.hebrew: והקריבה בארץ ישראל - שלא בירושלים. ולהכי נקט בא"י, דאף על גב דלא קיים נדרו יצא, דקביעותא דבית חוניו לאו קביעות הוא. (אלא היינו טעמא) דהוי כאומר על מנת שאהרגנה, ועל מנת שלא אתחייב באחריותה, דמה לי קטלה התם מה לי קטלה הכא. וענוש כרת משום שחוטי חוץ, אלמא שם עולה חל עלה כדרב המנונא:
Rashi on Menachot 109a:12:1.english: And he sacrificed it in the Land of Israel - Not in Jerusalem. And for this reason it specified "in the Land of Israel": for even though he did not fulfill his vow, he has fulfilled [his obligation], since the designation of the temple of Onias is not a [valid] designation. (Rather, this is the reason:) It is as if he says, "[It is incumbent upon me] on the condition that I kill it, and on the condition that I will not bear responsibility for it," for what difference does it make to me whether he killed it there, or what difference does it make to me whether he killed it here? And [the statement that] "he is punishable by excision" is on account of [the prohibition against] slaughtering offerings outside [the Temple]; thus, the status of a burnt offering took effect upon it, in accordance with [the view of] Rav Hamnuna.

Rashi on Menachot 109a:13:1.hebrew: במדבר - קסבר: משום משכן שהיה שם, יהא עדיין המדבר קדוש:
Rashi on Menachot 109a:13:1.english: In the wilderness - He thought [that] because of the Tabernacle that was there, the wilderness would still be sacred.

Rashi on Menachot 109a:13:2.hebrew: והקריבה בעבר הירדן - בארץ ישראל שלא בירושלים, אפי' הכי יצא, דעל מנת שלא אתחייב באחריות קאמר:
Rashi on Menachot 109a:13:2.english: And he sacrificed it across the Jordan - [Which is] in the Land of Israel, [yet] not in Jerusalem. Even so, he has fulfilled [his obligation], for [it is as if] he said: "On the condition that I will not bear liability [for it]."

Rashi on Menachot 109a:14:1.hebrew: ואין צריך לומר לדבר אחר - אם שמשו לעבודת כוכבים, לא ישמשו עוד בירושלים:
Rashi on Menachot 109a:14:1.english: And it is needless to say for another matter - If they served for idol worship, they may no longer serve in Jerusalem.

Rashi on Menachot 109a:14:2.hebrew: הרי אלו כבעלי מומין - שחולקין ואוכלין בקדשים, כדאמר באלו מנחות (לעיל מנחות עג.): איש חולק, ואפי' בעל מום:
Rashi on Menachot 109a:14:2.english: These are like blemished [priests] - That they receive a share and eat of the consecrated offerings, as [the Gemara] says in [the chapter] "Elu Menachot" (above, Menachot 73a): "A man receives a share," and even a blemished priest.

Rashi on Menachot 109a:15:1.hebrew: כהן ששחט בהמתו לעבודת כוכבים - לפני עבודת כוכבים, ושב, קרבנו שהוא מקריב במקדש אחרי כן, ריח ניחוח הוא:
Rashi on Menachot 109a:15:1.english: A priest who slaughtered his animal for idol worship - [That is,] before an idol, and he repented; his offering that he offers in the Temple afterward is a pleasing aroma.

Rashi on Menachot 109a:16:1.hebrew: אי עביד שירות - בעבודת כוכבים מיתסר במקדש, ושחיטה לא איקרי שירות, דהא במקדש כשרה בזר:
Rashi on Menachot 109a:16:1.english: If he performed service - [Only if he performed service] in idol worship is he forbidden [from serving] in the Temple, and slaughtering is not called "service," since in the Temple it is valid [even when performed] by a non-priest.

Rashi on Menachot 109a:17:1.hebrew: שגג בזריקה - זרק דם לעבודת כוכבים בשוגג, דהשתא עבד ליה שירות, אלא ששוגג היה:
Rashi on Menachot 109a:17:1.english: He erred in sprinkling - He sprinkled blood for idol worship unwittingly, for now he performed a service for it, only that he was unwitting.

Rashi on Menachot 109a:18:1.hebrew: מאי לאו או מכשול או עון - כלומר, או שוגג או מזיד עשו שירות לעבודת כוכבים, וכתיב: לא יגשו אלי לכהן לי:
Rashi on Menachot 109a:18:1.english: Is it not either a stumbling block or iniquity? - That is to say, [whether] unwittingly or intentionally, they performed service for idol worship, and it is written: "They shall not draw near to Me to serve Me as a priest."

Rashi on Menachot 109a:18:2.hebrew: עון מזיד - כדאמרי' במסכת יומא (דף לו:): עונות אלו הזדונות, וכן הוא אומר: הכרת תכרת עונה בה:
Rashi on Menachot 109a:18:2.english: "Iniquity" [means an] intentional [sin] - As we say in tractate Yoma (folio 36b): "'Iniquities' — these are intentional sins," and so it says: "[That person] shall be utterly cut off, his iniquity is upon him."

Rashi on Menachot 109a:1:1.hebrew: ואמאי ניחזי הי נפיל - אי גדול נפל, הפסיד לוקח, דהא גדול שבבתים משמע. ואי קטן נפל, לית ליה פסידא:
Rashi on Menachot 109a:1:1.english: And why? Let us see which [one] fell - If the large [one] fell, the buyer has lost [out], for [the expression] implies the largest of the houses. And if the small [one] fell, he has no loss.

Rashi on Menachot 109a:20:1.hebrew: בחטאה בשגגה - משמע אפי' נפש כהן, בחטאה בשגגה יכול להקריב קרבנו ולהקריב על עצמו. ובההיא פרשתא בעבודת כוכבים מישתעי, כדכתיב (במדבר טו) וכי תשגו ולא תעשו וגו', זו עבודת כוכבים ששקולה כנגד כל התורה כולה:
Rashi on Menachot 109a:20:1.english: When it sins unwittingly - [This] implies [that] even [if] the person [is] a priest, when he sins unwittingly he may offer his sacrifice and sacrifice on his own behalf. And that passage speaks of idolatry, as it is written (Numbers 15[:22]): "And when you shall err, and not observe..." etc. — this is idolatry, which is equivalent to the entire Torah.

Rashi on Menachot 109a:21:1.hebrew: במאי - פלח לעבודת כוכבים, דאיצטריך קרא לאכשורי לעבוד במקדש כי שגג:
Rashi on Menachot 109a:21:1.english: In what - [manner did he] worship idols, that a verse was needed to qualify him to serve in the Temple when he acted unwittingly?

Rashi on Menachot 109a:2:1.hebrew: בעל השטר - כגון האי לוקח שבא בשטר מכירה, ידו על התחתונה, דהוי מוציא מחבירו, עליו הראיה, שהמוכר מוחזק בבתים. הלכך ראיה על הלוקח, אבל גבי הקדש גדול משמע:
Rashi on Menachot 109a:2:1.english: The holder of the document - For example, this buyer who comes with a deed of sale, his hand is at a disadvantage, as he is [in the position of] one who extracts [property] from his fellow, [and upon him] rests the burden of proof, since the seller is in possession of the houses. Therefore, [the burden of] proof rests upon the buyer, but regarding consecrated property, [the term] implies [the] large [one].

Rashi on Menachot 109a:4:1.hebrew: שאקריבנה בבית חוניו יקריבנה במקדש - דכיון דאמר הרי עלי עולה, איחייב ליה בעולה:
Rashi on Menachot 109a:4:1.english: [That] I will offer it in the House of Chonyo (Onias), he must offer it in the Temple - For since he said "It is incumbent upon me [to bring] a burnt offering," he has become obligated in a burnt offering.

Rashi on Menachot 109a:4:2.english: If he sacrificed it in the temple of Onias, he has fulfilled [his obligation] - The reason is explained in the Gemara.

Rashi on Menachot 109a:5:1.english: He shall shave in the Temple - [That is, he] brings his offerings [there].

Rashi on Menachot 109a:6:1.hebrew: והא מקטל קטלה - דשוחט חוץ הוא, ואיהו איחייב בעולה מכי אמר הרי עלי עולה:
Rashi on Menachot 109a:6:1.english: But hasn't he [merely] killed it - For he is one who slaughters outside [the Temple], and he became obligated in a burnt offering from [the moment] he said, "It is incumbent upon me [to bring] a burnt offering."

Rashi on Menachot 109a:7:1.hebrew: אמר רב המנונא - כיון דאמר על מנת שאקריבנה בבית חוניו, הוי כאילו אמר על מנת שאהרגנה, ולא איתחייב באחריותה, ומשום הכי יצא. אבל חייב כרת משום שחוטי חוץ, שהרי קרא עליה שם עולה:
Rashi on Menachot 109a:7:1.english: Rav Hamnuna said - Since he said, "on the condition that I sacrifice it in the House of Onias (Beit Chonyo)," it is as though he said, "on the condition that I kill it," and he did not obligate himself to responsibility for it, and because of this he has fulfilled [his obligation]. But he is liable to excision (karet) for [slaughtering] offerings outside [the Temple], for he indeed designated the status of a burnt offering upon it.

Rashi on Menachot 109a:8:1.hebrew: נזיר לא מצי לאתנויי על מנת שלא אתחייב באחריות דקרבנותיו, דכיון דחלה עליו נזירות, לא פקעא מיניה עד דמייתי קרבנותיו:
Rashi on Menachot 109a:8:1.english: A nazirite cannot stipulate: "On the condition that I will not bear responsibility for my offerings," because once naziriteship has taken effect upon him, it does not leave him until he brings his offerings.

Rashi on Menachot 109a:9:1.english: He intended [it] merely as a gift - And the status of a burnt offering did not take effect upon it.

Rashi on Menachot 109a:9:2.hebrew: טפי לא מצינא לאיצטעורי - ברחוק מארץ ישראל עומד וקרוב לחוניו, ואליבא דרבא לא מחייב משום שחוטי חוץ:
Rashi on Menachot 109a:9:2.english: More [than this], I cannot trouble myself - He is standing far from the Land of Israel and close to [the temple of] Chonyo (Onias), and according to Rava, he is not liable on account of [the prohibition against] slaughtering outside [the Temple].

Tosafot on Menachot 109a:14:1.hebrew: לא ישמשו במקדש בירושלים - בספר הזהיר כתוב: כהן שהמיר דתו לא ישא את כפיו ולא יקרא ראשון, דכתיב: "וקדשתו", והוא אחליה לקדושתיה, ועבדו ליה רבנן מעלה מפני דרכי שלום, והאי כיון דאידחי אידחי, כדתנן: הכהנים ששמשו בבית חוניו לא ישמשו במקדש שבירושלים. ורש"י פירש דכשר, וזה לשונו: הרי אלו כבעלי מומין כו' - מהכא נפקא לן דכהן שהמיר דתו וחזר בתשובה כשר לדוכן, שהרי לא מצינו כהן בעל מום שיהא פסול לדוכן, אלא אם היה לו מום בידיו, כדאמרינן במגילה (דף כד:) מפני שהעם מסתכלין בו. ותו, הא דקתני: לא ישמשו במקדש בירושלים, ולהכי איצטריך בירושלים לאשמועינן דבנוב וגבעון היו מותרין לשמש, כל שכן בזמן הזה, שאין שירות ואין מקדש, דודאי כשר לדוכן ולקרות בתורה תחילה. ותו אמרינן (תענית דף כז.): אי מה משרת בעל מום לא, אף מברך בעל מום לא? ת"ל: לעמוד לשרת, לעמידה הקשתיו ולא לדבר אחר, עד כאן לשונו:
Tosafot on Menachot 109a:14:1.english: They may not serve in the Temple in Jerusalem - In the Sefer HaZahir it is written: A kohen who apostatized may not lift his hands [to recite the Priestly Blessing] and may not read [from the Torah] first, as it is written: "And you shall sanctify him" (Leviticus 21:8) — but he profaned his sanctity. And the Rabbis instituted an additional stringency on account of the ways of peace [that a kohen is called first to the Torah], and this person, once he was disqualified, remains disqualified, as we learned in the Mishnah: "The kohanim who served in the House of Chonyo may not serve in the Temple in Jerusalem." And Rashi explained that he is valid, and this is his wording: "'These are like blemished priests, etc.' — From here we derive that a kohen who apostatized and repented is fit for the duchan [the platform for the Priestly Blessing]. For we do not find that a blemished kohen (ba'al mum) is disqualified from the duchan, unless he had a blemish on his hands, as we say in Megillah (24b), because the people gaze at him. And furthermore, that which it teaches: 'They may not serve in the Temple in Jerusalem' — and for this reason 'in Jerusalem' was necessary, to teach us that at Nov and Giv'on they would have been permitted to serve — all the more so in the present time, when there is no sacrificial service and no Temple, that he is certainly fit for the duchan and to read first from the Torah. And furthermore, we say (Ta'anit 27a): 'If [you suggest that] just as one who ministers may not be a blemished priest, so too one who blesses may not be a blemished priest? Scripture states: "to stand to minister" (Deuteronomy 18:5) — I compared it [the blessing] to it [service] with regard to standing, but not with regard to anything else.' Thus far his words."

Tosafot on Menachot 109a:15:1.hebrew: כהן ששחט לעבודת כוכבים קרבנו ריח ניחוח - ולרב ששת בשוגג, ולרב נחמן אפי' במזיד:
Tosafot on Menachot 109a:15:1.english: A priest who slaughtered for idol worship, his offering is a pleasing aroma - And according to Rav Sheshet, [this refers to a case where he did so] unwittingly (beshogeg), and according to Rav Nachman, even intentionally (bemezid).

Tosafot on Menachot 109a:3:1.hebrew: אפילו תימא עלייה דגריעה יד בעל השטר על התחתונה - תימה, דבפ' הנודר מן הירק (נדרים נו.) מסיק: מאי עלייה? מעולה שבנכסיו. ושמא דיחויא הוא. אבל קשיא, דמסיק: יד בעל השטר על העליונה. ושמא לאפוקי יציע דווקא קאתי:
Tosafot on Menachot 109a:3:1.english: Even if you say an upper story is inferior, the holder of the document has the lower hand - This is surprising, for in the chapter "HaNoder Min HaYarak" (Nedarim 56a) it concludes: What is an aliyah? The finest of his property. And perhaps that was [merely] a dismissal. But it is difficult, for it concludes that the holder of the document has the upper hand. And perhaps it comes specifically to exclude a lean-to (yatzia).

Tosafot on Menachot 109a:4:1.hebrew: שאקריבנה בבית חוניו - אין שייך כאן תפוס לשון ראשון ואחרון, דהוי כאומר: עד בית חוניו מצינא דאטרח, כדאיתא בגמ':
Tosafot on Menachot 109a:4:1.english: That I will sacrifice it in the temple of Onias - [The rule of] seizing upon the first formulation or the last (tefos lashon rishon ve-acharon) does not apply here, for it is as though he is saying: "As far as the temple of Onias I am able to exert myself," as stated in the Gemara.
